correctness.rationale: For strictly positive g,A,b,k,h,p,c,delta with A>b, define sigma=delta/c, a(y)=A/(1+k y), G(y)=g/(1+k y)-h-p y. Predator-positive equilibria have u+v=sigma; subtraction of the two per-capita prey balances gives (b-a(y))(u-v)=0. Strict monotonicity of the symmetric and exclusion scalar growth equations gives exactly one positive symmetric equilibrium iff g>g0=h+(A+b)sigma/2 and two predator-positive exclusion states iff g>g1=h+A sigma, with g0<g1<gc=(1+k yc)(h+p yc+b sigma), yc=(A/b-1)/k. Asymmetry with both prey positive requires a(y)=b and G(y)=b sigma, forcing g=gc and the entire segment (u,v,yc), u+v=sigma. At the symmetric state the exchange eigenvalue sigma(b-a(ys))/2 changes negative to positive across gc, and its other eigenvalues solve a quadratic with positive linear and constant coefficients. Boundary invasion eigenvalue sigma(a(yb)-b) changes positive to negative; the other pair remains Hurwitz. At gc the full Jacobian has a simple zero eigenvalue tangent to the line and normal polynomial L^2+b*sigma L+c*yc*sigma*D(w), D(w)=p+k[gc-A*sigma(1+w^2)/2]/(1+k yc)^2 >p, uniformly for -1<=w<=1 because gc>A*sigma. This proves normal attraction, including endpoints; points on the continuum are not individually asymptotically stable. Independently reconstructed the full vector field/Jacobian and symbolically verified line field=0 and its characteristic quadratic for all parameters; computed stable nonzero spectra for two distinct rational positive parameter sets and five positions per segment. Read rather than trusted the source check.py, its claims and a sample; finite numerical tests do not establish the unrestricted theorem. No global claim is inferred.

value.rationale: PASS: The exact equality A/(1+k y)=b marks a natural ecological exchange between within-prey and cross-prey suppression generated by predator fear. The model-specific classification determines when a symmetric coexistence fixed point, two single-prey predator-positive states, and a continuum of neutral prey-composition states exist, with the complete local spectra and a sharp threshold gc. This supplies a motivated infinite-parameter bifurcation boundary and identifies a normally attracting equilibrium manifold rather than an isolated pitchfork; its endpoint and stable-branch information is mathematically usable even without global dynamics. It is substantially more than a numerical example or restating a standard eigenvalue criterion, though derivation uses elementary ODE methods and the symmetry is nongeneric. No claim of global basins or asymmetry robustness.
